newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean business body to send corn to North.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean business body to send corn to North.

text.p: The Federation of Korean Industries, which represents South Korea's leading businesses, said on Thursday it would send $2 million worth of corn to famine-threatened North Korea.
A statement said the shipment of 11,000 tonnes of corn would be delivered via South Korea's Red Cross.

"Our members agreed at a meeting that any support to our brethren in North Korea should be made on condition it contributes to improving South-North Korean relations and gives real help to North Korean citizens," the statement said.
The federation represents almost all of the country's top 30 industrial conglomerates, known as "chaebol", including the giant Samsung, Hyundai and Daewoo groups.
South Korean businesses face severe government restrictions on investment in North Korea.

On Wednesday, South Korea's Red Cross said it would donate 1,000 tonnes of flour to the North worth 350 million won ($392,000). Inter-Korean Red Cross talks on speeding up food aid are due to start in Beijing on Friday.
